metadata.title: The development and validation of the Multidimensional Assessment of Teacher Social-Emotional Competence (MATSEC) in East Asian school contexts
metadata.venue: Social and Emotional Learning: Research, Practice, and Policy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study collected teacher survey data in two countries (China and South Korea) using a stratified cluster random sampling approach in one Chinese county and convenience sampling via teacher associations in Korea. The analysis is psychometric (EFA/CFA, bifactor/second-order models, measurement invariance) rather than an achievement-score ILSA analysis, and the manuscript does not report the use of complex survey weights or any weight variable names. Because no PV-based achievement outcomes are modeled and no survey-weighted estimation is described, there is no explicit guidance on which sampling weight (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply. For users who want population-representative inference, the absence of documented weights and the Korea convenience sample limit generalizability beyond the sampled teacher populations.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because the study develops and validates a teacher self-report scale (MATSEC/T-SEC) using factor-analytic psychometrics rather than PV-based cognitive achievement scores from an ILSA. Missing-data handling is largely described at the descriptive level (no missing data in major variables except 13 cases for Chinese sociodemographics), but the manuscript does not provide a full, explicit missing-data procedure for all analyses (e.g., whether any cases were excluded for CFA/EFA). This is therefore a reporting gap for the analytic pipeline rather than a PV-related issue.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Main study (Spring 2024): included teachers employed in regular schools during the Spring semester, restricted to elementary schools in both countries and middle schools in China only; excluded principals/vice-principals, teachers in special schools primarily serving students with disabilities, and teachers on leave as of Spring 2024. China sample: recruited from the same individuals as the Fall 2023 pilot, using stratified cluster random sampling within one southwestern China county (20 elementary and 20 middle schools; within-school stratification by grade, homeroom role, and gender). Korea sample: convenience sampling via nationwide teacher associations/online communities; eligibility verified via an active professional email address provided during consent. Analytic sample for factor validation: entire sample N=859 was split using the SOLOMON technique into EFA subsample n=430 and CFA subsample n=429; EFA used principal axis factoring with Promax rotation and CFA used robust maximum likelihood (MLR).

main_findings.dataset_used: MATSEC teacher survey (Spring 2024) — China (elementary) and South Korea (elementary) — T-SEC scale validation
main_findings.performance_metrics: EFA/CFA fit and reliability: Model 4 (27 items, six-factor) CFA fit χ2=520.79, df=309, CFI=0.96, TLI=0.95, RMSEA=0.05, SRMR=0.04. Second-order model (Model 5) fit (entire sample N=859): χ2=751.04, df=318, CFI=0.95, TLI=0.95, RMSEA=0.05, SRMR=0.04; McDonald’s omega: first-order factors 0.82–0.91, second-order factor ω=0.94. Bifactor model (Model 6) fit (entire sample): χ2=688.97, df=297, CFI=0.96, TLI=0.95, RMSEA=0.05, SRMR=0.04; general factor ω=0.97, ωH=0.92; dimensionality indices ECV=0.75, PUC=0.85, ARPB=3%. Measurement invariance across CHN vs KOR: ΔCFI<0.01, ΔTLI<0.01, ΔRMSEA<0.01, ΔSRMR≤0.015.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using MATSEC teacher survey (Spring 2024) data from China (elementary) and South Korea (elementary) to validate the T-SEC scale, the study leveraged mental well-being, teacher self-efficacy, teacher burnout, school climate, and job satisfaction as concurrent validity anchors, finding that the MATSEC supports an overarching higher-order T-SEC factor with six sub-factors and strong internal consistency (omega general factor ω=0.97; ωH=0.92) plus strong cross-country measurement invariance. This indicates that a CASEL-aligned, equity-and-inclusion–enhanced teacher SEL competence measure can be used comparably across East Asian contexts for research and professional development needs assessment, while the results are limited to self-report and cross-sectional validation.

data.outcome_summary: This paper develops and validates the Multidimensional Assessment of Teacher Social-Emotional Competence (MATSEC) using teacher self-report survey data collected in Spring 2024 from 859 teachers in China (CHN, n=602; elementary) and South Korea (KOR, n=257; elementary). The authors used a psychometric pipeline (EFA on n=430 and CFA on n=429 via the SOLOMON split) and compared non-hierarchical, second-order, and bifactor models, reporting strong model fit (e.g., bifactor Model 6 on the full sample: χ2=688.97, df=297, CFI=0.96, TLI=0.95, RMSEA=0.05, SRMR=0.04). Reliability was high for the general factor (ω=0.97; ωH=0.92) and dimensionality indices supported unidimensional measurement of the overarching construct (ECV=0.75, PUC=0.85, ARPB=3%). Concurrent validity correlations were moderate-to-strong (overall T-SEC r≈0.42–0.65 with most anchors; negative with depression/anxiety and burnout). Limitations include self-report measurement, cross-sectional design, and Korea’s convenience sampling, which constrain generalizability.
